1º de Primaria · Inglés

My body

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Touch your head. Now touch your nose. Do you know these words in English?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Head is cabeza and nose is nariz. In this unit you will learn the names of the parts of your body.

2

Aprende12 apartados

Para empezar: The monster drawing

Max and Zoe are drawing a monster in art class.

«My monster has got three eyes!» says Max. He draws three big eyes.

«My monster has got four arms», says Zoe. «And six legs!»

Max adds a big mouth and two small ears. Zoe adds a long, purple nose.

The teacher laughs. «What a funny monster! How many hands has it got?»

Max and Zoe count: «One, two, three, four. Four hands!» The monster waves all its hands. Hello!

1. My body

This is my body. It is amazing!

My body helps me run, jump, eat and play.

In this unit, we are going to learn the names of the parts of the body. Stand up and move your body!

2. Head, arms and legs

On top of my body is my head.

I have two arms and two legs.

I move my arms to swim. I move my legs to walk and run. Wave your arms! Shake your legs!

3. Hands and feet

At the end of my arms are my hands. At the end of my legs are my feet.

One hand, two hands. One foot, two feet! Foot is special: the plural is feet.

I clap my hands. I stamp my feet.

4. Fingers and toes

I have ten fingers on my hands.

I have ten toes on my feet.

Let's count our fingers: one, two, three… ten! Now wiggle your toes. Can you count them too?

5. My face

My face is on my head. On my face I have two eyes, a nose and a mouth.

I see with my eyes. I smell with my nose. I eat and talk with my mouth.

Point to your eyes. Point to your nose!

Vídeo: My Body Parts: Head to Toes · English Singsing (YouTube) · 39,3 millones de visualizaciones

6. Ears and hair

I have two ears. I hear music with my ears.

On my head I have hair. Hair can be short or long. It can be black, brown, blond or red.

What colour is your hair? My hair is brown.

7. I've got…

To talk about our body, we say I've got… or I have…

I've got two eyes. I've got short hair. I have ten fingers.

Describe yourself to a friend!

8. Touch your head!

Let's play! Listen and touch.

Touch your head! Touch your nose! Touch your knees! Touch your toes!

Now sing the famous song: Head, shoulders, knees and toes! Faster and faster!

Vídeo: Me! | Songs For Children · Noodle & Pals (YouTube) · 62,5 millones de visualizaciones

9. My senses

My body has five senses.

I see with my eyes. I hear with my ears. I smell with my nose.

I taste with my mouth. I touch with my hands. Our senses tell us about the world.

10. Take care of your body

We must take care of our body.

Wash your hands. Brush your teeth. Eat fruit. Sleep well.

Exercise is good too: run, jump and dance every day. A happy body is a healthy body!

11. Game: the monster

Draw a monster! Roll a dice.

Number 1: draw eyes. Number 2: draw arms. Number 3: draw legs… Roll again to know how many!

Then describe it: My monster has got three eyes and four arms!

12. Review: my body

Now you know your body in English: head, arms, legs, hands, feet, fingers and toes.

You know your face: eyes, ears, nose, mouth and hair.

You can say I've got… and play Touch your…! Fantastic!

Lo hacemos juntos · Let's do it together

How many eyes have you got?

  1. Touch your eyes.
  2. Count: one, two.
  3. Start with: I've got…

Resultado: I've got two eyes.

The teacher says: Touch your ears!

  1. Listen: ears.
  2. Ears are for hearing.
  3. Touch them with your hands.

Resultado: You touch your ears.

One foot, two…

  1. Foot is a special word.
  2. The plural is not «foots».

Resultado: two feet.

What do you do with your nose?

  1. Think of the five senses.
  2. The nose smells flowers and food.

Resultado: I smell with my nose.

Errores típicos

  • Saying «two foots»: the plural of foot is feet.
  • Saying «I've got blue eye»: we have two, so we say «blue eyes».
  • Mixing up «hair» and «head»: hair grows on your head.
  • Saying «my nose» like Spanish «nos»: in English it sounds like «nous».

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (22)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Touch your head.

    Ver solución
    The child touches the head.

  2. Touch your nose.

    Ver solución
    The child touches the nose.

  3. Point to your eyes and say: eyes.

    Ver solución
    Eyes.

  4. Clap your hands three times.

    Ver solución
    Clap, clap, clap.

  5. Stamp your feet!

    Ver solución
    The child stamps the feet.

  6. Draw a face with two eyes, a nose and a mouth.

    Ver solución
    A simple face.

  7. Match: mano – hand, pie – foot.

    Ver solución
    Hand = mano; foot = pie.

  8. How many fingers on one hand?

    Ver solución
    Five.

Nivel medio

  1. Complete: I've got two ____ (ojos).

    Ver solución
    eyes.

  2. Complete: I've got ten ____ (dedos de las manos).

    Ver solución
    fingers.

  3. What do you hear with?

    Ver solución
    With my ears.

  4. One foot, two ____.

    Ver solución
    feet.

  5. Describe your hair: My hair is…

    Ver solución
    Free answer, for example: My hair is short and brown.

  6. Play «Simon says» with three body parts.

    Ver solución
    For example: Simon says touch your knees!

  7. Sing «Head, shoulders, knees and toes» and touch each part.

    Ver solución
    Free answer.

  8. Write two things you do to take care of your body.

    Ver solución
    Wash my hands, brush my teeth (free answer).

  9. Draw yourself and label: head, arm, leg.

    Ver solución
    A self-portrait with three labels.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Draw a monster and describe it: My monster has got…

    Ver solución
    Free answer, for example: three eyes and four arms.

  2. Match the senses: see – eyes, hear – ears, smell – nose, taste – mouth, touch – hands.

    Ver solución
    See: eyes; hear: ears; smell: nose; taste: mouth; touch: hands.

  3. Describe a friend: He's got / She's got…

    Ver solución
    Free answer, for example: She's got long hair.

  4. Count all the fingers and toes in your family.

    Ver solución
    Free answer: 20 for each person.

  5. Invent a new verse for the song: «Eyes and ears and mouth and nose».

    Ver solución
    Free answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeThe life-size body poster

We draw around a classmate on big paper and label the body parts in English for our classroom wall.

Pasos

  1. One child lies on a big sheet of paper. A friend draws around the body.
  2. In groups, we colour the body and draw the face.
  3. We write labels in English: head, arm, leg, hand, foot, eyes, ears, nose, mouth.
  4. We play «Touch your…!» pointing to the poster.

Producto final: A life-size body poster with labels in English.

Cómo se valora

  • Names the parts of the body in English.
  • Places each label in the right place.
  • Follows Touch your… instructions.

Resumen visualTodo el tema en una pantalla

Glosario

Body
All of you, from head to feet (cuerpo).
Head
The top part of your body (cabeza).
Arm
You have two; they end in hands (brazo).
Leg
You walk with your legs (pierna).
Hand
It has five fingers (mano).
Foot
It has five toes; two are feet (pie).
Eyes
You see with your eyes (ojos).
Ears
You hear with your ears (orejas).
Nose
You smell with your nose (nariz).
Mouth
You eat and talk with your mouth (boca).
6

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Jugad a «Simon says: touch your…» en casa.
  • Al bañarle, nombrad las partes del cuerpo en inglés.
  • Cantad «Head, shoulders, knees and toes» cada vez más rápido.
  • Dibujad juntos un monstruo y describidlo: «It's got three eyes!».

Para profesores

Saberes: Lengua extranjera (Inglés): léxico del cuerpo y la cara; estructuras I've got… / I have…; plurales regulares e irregulares (feet); instrucciones con respuesta física; hábitos saludables (RD 157/2022, primer ciclo de Educación Primaria).

  • Canciones de acción (Head, shoulders, knees and toes) con movimiento.
  • Silueta a tamaño real con etiquetas en inglés.
  • Juego del monstruo con dados.
  • Relación con Ciencias: los cinco sentidos.

Fuentes y revisión

  • Real Decreto 157/2022, enseñanzas mínimas de la Educación Primaria (BOE)

Revisado el 14 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name parts of the body: head, arms, legs, hands, feet
  • Name parts of the face: eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hair
  • Use I have… and I've got…
  • Count body parts: two eyes, ten fingers
  • Follow action songs: touch your head, clap your hands

Palabras clave

body · head · arm · leg · hand · foot · eyes · ears · nose · mouth · touch

Tiempo

50 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
